title: Latency-tiered phase partitioner with kernel-cost feedback
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
We need a prefill/decode scheduling policy that dynamically partitions request phases into latency tiers using live kernel-cost feedback from the runtime. The goal is to reduce p95/p99 tail latency for latency-sensitive customers while preserving throughput for best-effort workloads and maintaining proportional fairness across tenants. This ticket implements the scheduler component and experiment harness for production evaluation.

Problem statement:
Current phase-based schedulers assume static cost models for kernel selection and treat all prefill/decode phases with the same priority buckets. Two practical issues arise: (1) kernel execution cost varies by model, sequence length, and runtime kernel choice (e.g., fused-attn vs generic), and (2) mixed workloads (chat vs batch embeddings) create conflicting objectives between latency and throughput. We need a scheduler that co-optimizes scheduling decisions with live kernel-cost observations to avoid starvation of low-cost requests and prevent high-cost phases from amplifying tail latency.

Goals:
- Integrate a lightweight kernel-cost estimator into the arbitration loop (no full recompiles).
- Partition incoming prefill/decode work into latency tiers (e.g., FAST, STANDARD, BULK) based on SLA, observed kernel cost, and historical service times.
- Apply hedged re-dispatch and opportunistic fast-paths for FAST-tier while allowing bulk consolidation for BULK-tier to preserve throughput.
- Maintain proportional fairness quotas across customers over a sliding window to prevent long-term starvation.
- Provide feature flags and metrics to A/B test behavior before broad rollout.

Approach:
1) Kernel-cost feedback: augment runtime to emit a compact per-request kernel_cost estimate (normalized device-ms). The scheduler consumes a 1s sliding window to compute per-model and per-sequence-length cost distributions.
2) Latency-tier assignment: combine request SLA hints (client-provided priority header), current kernel_cost percentile (p50/p75), and queue wait-time to compute a score and map to FAST/STANDARD/BULK. FAST-tier gets hedged replication (short-hedge only when queue wait > threshold) and preferential microbatch packing algorithm tuned to preserve low tail latency.
3) Fairness controller: track per-tenant budget consumption (cost-weighted) over 5-minute windows; if a tenant exceeds its fair share, move lower-priority requests to BULK-tier until budget recovers.
4) Kernel-aware batching: for BULK-tier, prefer packing requests with compatible kernel profiles to maximize fused-kernel utilization. This reorders work opportunistically but respects end-to-end SLAs when assigned.

Trade-offs considered:
- Accuracy vs overhead of kernel_cost signal: we use a short aggregation window to avoid oscillation; instrumentation cost is <0.5% CPU in probe runs.
- Hedging increases duplicate work but targeted to FAST-tier with strict caps to bound cost impact.
- Opportunistic reordering risks small latency regressions for STANDARD-tier; mitigated by conservative thresholds and canary rollout.

Experiment plan and success metrics:
- A/B canary on engdedicated-1 GPU pool for 2 weeks.
- Targets vs baseline: p95 latency for FAST-tier down 20% and p99 down 15% under mixed load (chat + embeddings); overall throughput drop <= 5% at 95th percentile. Cost-per-token increase for FAST hedging <= 7% (acceptable for SLAed customers).
- Fairness: long-run cost-weighted share deviation across tenants < 5% over a 15-minute window.

Implementation notes:
- Scheduler change will be implemented in runtime arbiter module (scheduler/smart_partitioner.cc). New socket for kernel_cost events: Runtime -> Arbiter via existing stats channel.
- Feature flags: runtime.scheduler.latency_tiers.enabled, runtime.scheduler.kernel_feedback.window_ms, runtime.scheduler.hedge_caps.per_minute.
- Add telemetry: metric names runtime.scheduler.tier_assignment, runtime.scheduler.kernel_cost.p50,p75,p95 (by model), runtime.scheduler.hedge_rate, runtime.scheduler.fairness_violation_count.

Rollout plan:
- Dev integration and unit tests (week 1)
- Canary on test pool + guardrails (week 2)
- Broader canary with 10% of production traffic behind feature flag (week 3)
- Full rollout conditional on metrics and SRE signoff (week 4)

Notes on backward compatibility:
- If runtime does not emit kernel_cost, policy falls back to static heuristics (sequence length + model table). No behavioral change for customers until feature flag enabled.

Open questions:
- How aggressive should packing be for BULK-tier when model kernels are incompatible? (See comment thread for simulation results.)
- Should we allow customers to opt out of hedging due to cost sensitivity? (Design proposes header opt-out but needs PM decision.)
acceptance_criteria: Kernel-cost signal ingested by arbiter and visible in test telemetry
Unit/integration tests for fairness controller and hedging caps
Canary run shows p95 FAST-tier improvement >= 15% with <=5% throughput regression
Rollout playbook and rollback triggers documented in Confluence

comments: 2026-02-21 Miguel: Spike completed. Kernel_cost signal implemented as an additional uint16 estimate; emits per-request in metrics stream. Overhead measured ~0.3% on probe workload.
2026-02-25 Priya: Fairness controller draft implemented. Uses token-bucket style budget weighted by kernel_cost. Need to tune refill rate based on traffic patterns.

2026-03-01 Brandon: Simulation results attached show that packing incompatible kernels in BULK-tier reduces throughput by ~8% for small batches; recommend thresholding by compatibility score >= 0.65. See simulation: https://internal-runs/reports/33111-sim
2026-03-05 Design review (Ana): UX for SLA hint header approved; suggest adding explicit customer opt-out for hedging. Forwarding to PM for decision.
2026-03-09 Miguel: PR opened for arbiter changes - https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1247. Initial CI failures relate to flaky timing test; investigating.
2026-03-12 SRE comment (Ravi): Canary runbook needs explicit rollback triggers: >10% p95 regression for STANDARD-tier OR >10% cost increase for FAST hedging. Added to playbook.
2026-03-13 Aisha: Kernel_cost p50/p75 telemetry added to staging dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/runtime/33111-kernel-cost
